design_condition: Set back from the street and stepped toward the smaller residential edge, the building forms a large southwest forecourt, roof terraces, and multiple connections to the surrounding area.

positive.statement: The project makes a clear statement on the street and responds subtly to the heterogeneous urban situation.
The large forecourt forms the heart of the campus and creates a clear address.
The setbacks create an appropriate transition to the small-scale residential surroundings.
The side entrances provide an optimal connection to the surrounding area.
The entrance hall forms an inviting start to the route through the building.
The clerestory brings daylight and creates visual connections to the sports area.
The classrooms are well proportioned and clearly arranged.
The project implements the spatial program in an extremely space-efficient and resource-saving manner.
The facade design ties the upper floors together and closes the building at the top.

negative.statement: The roof terraces are unfortunately reserved for the respective classrooms.
The tower-like staircase does not seem energetically resolved with the glass blocks.
The complex static system significantly limits flexibility for later changes of use.
The permissible building dimensions are clearly exceeded.
Some spatial geometries appear to have only limited use for school operations.
The stepped form produces unfavorable compactness and a comparatively high heating requirement is expected.
The terrace windows are likely to provide little comfort in the cold season.
The open space is too reserved and does not exploit the potential of the forecourt as an attractive entrance.
